audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Olaf levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items and gave level 6 to Skill. The matchup's own whys say levels 4-5 'finally stabilize the lane' (Skill), level 6 is 'your spike' (Cho'Gath), and first item is 'neither side cleanly snowballs' (Skill).
audit.why: Feast at 6 is the only thing in Cho'Gath's kit that beats an Olaf who has stacked resistances off Ragnarok's passive; before that his axe-slow chain owns the lane and after two items his lifesteal and true damage take it back.
audit.corrected: Olaf / Olaf / Olaf / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Olaf — matching the packet chart. Proposed as one atomic group across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side+rating.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase text listed 'levels 2-3 (full pattern)' and Heartsteel as Cho'Gath's spikes, and said to 'force fights the moment it completes'.
audit.why: Levels 2-3 are Olaf's strongest window in this lane, not Cho'Gath's, and the first-item timing is where the duel is merely even. The only Cho'Gath spike that changes the fight is Feast at 6.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].why rewritten to the real timeline; first item downgraded from a fight-forcing spike to parity.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two ability facts are wrong across five fields. (1) Olaf's W is called 'Vicious Strikes' and credited with lifesteal in spikes[3], late, whys[5], whys[6] and wants.foe[2]. His W is Tough It Out — attack speed and a shield. The lifesteal comes from Berserker Rage (P), scaling with missing health. (2) Ragnarok is repeatedly described as giving 'flat damage reduction' in spikes[1], mid, whys[4] and wants.you[1]. Riot's text gives it bonus armour and magic resist passively, plus disable immunity on activation — no damage reduction.
audit.why: Vicious Strikes is an out-of-date name for that slot, exactly the class of error this audit exists to kill. The Ragnarok wording matters because the reason Feast still works is that true damage ignores resistances — a genuine damage-reduction effect would apply to true damage too, so the wrong wording also breaks the reasoning.
audit.corrected: W renamed to Tough It Out and the lifesteal reattributed to Berserker Rage (P); Ragnarok's benefit restated as bonus armour and MR, which is precisely what Feast's true damage bypasses.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was placeholder text with no numbers, and Undertow's defining property was absent.
audit.why: Undertow is nominally 9s but the cooldown resets the moment Olaf picks the axe back up, so 'wait out his Q' is bad advice unless you are between him and the axe. Ragnarok is 100s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Both written in, along with Reckless Swing at 11s rank 1.

audit.why: Armour plus Plated Steelcaps and early Grievous Wounds is right here — Olaf is physical damage and his sustain is lifesteal — so I left the itemization row alone. Worth keeping the caveat that neither armour nor anti-heal touches Reckless Swing's true damage, which I added to dosFull[1].d.

notes: Highest-value correction in this matchup: Olaf's W is named 'Vicious Strikes' and credited with lifesteal in five separate fields. Riot's current data has W = Tough It Out (attack speed + shield) and the lifesteal on Berserker Rage (P). I fixed the five fields I could reach inside the length band; the 'mid' and 'late' prose blocks also carry the same two errors ('Vicious Strikes' in late, 'flat damage reduction on Ragnarok' in mid) but rewriting those two long blocks inside +/-10% while keeping everything else they say correct was not something I could do without cutting real content, so they need a second pass. NOT ASSERTED: whether Feast can be cast on Olaf during Ragnarok (Ragnarok grants immunity to disables — whether Riot classes Feast's suppression-style devour as a disable is not in the kit data and needsResearch is null), and whether Undertow's armour shred stacks with itself. That first question is the single most decisive unknown in this lane and I left every Feast-during-Ragnarok claim out of the text rather than guess.
